subject: Private deployment: networking clarifications and next technical deep-dive
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@aurelia.ai>, ops@aurelia.ai
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: networking clarifications and next technical deep-dive

Hi Daniel / Aurelia ops team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — good to hear where you are on the evaluation. Per our discussion, it sounds like Aurelia is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (private control plane + customer-managed network) to satisfy data residency and isolation requirements. Below is a concise recap of the networking items we need to qualify before we lock the design and schedule the engineering deep-dive: 

1) Connectivity preference: PrivateLink (endpoint in your VPC) vs VPC Peering (direct network route). You mentioned a preference for endpoint-based connectivity but wanted to confirm limitations around cross-account endpoints.
2) Egress model: Will outbound requests from Redwood to your services be over PrivateLink, peered routes, or via a customer NAT? We also need to confirm whether you require static egress IPs on our side (we can provide static ranges for Dedicated/Private but hosted routes differ).
3) IP allowlist: List of CIDR ranges or individual IPs your network team will allow. If you prefer, a spreadsheet template is attached for your ops team to fill.
4) TLS / mTLS and authentication: Are you expecting mutual TLS, token-based bearer auth, or IAM-style certs?
5) KMS / key handling: If you need our private deployment to integrate with your KMS/HSM, please indicate provider and key rotation windows.
6) Audit & logs: Required retention window and whether audit logs must be forwarded to your SIEM (we can forward to an S3 bucket or syslog endpoint).

I've attached our Private VPC checklist to make this easier to walk through (redwood-priv-vpc-checklist.pdf). Proposed next step: a 60-min technical deep-dive with Ben (our SE) and Karthik (solutions) to go line-by-line on day/time that works for you. Can you share a 2-hour window next week and the best network contact (name/email) we should include?

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

[attachment: redwood-priv-vpc-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@aurelia.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@aurelia.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: networking clarifications and next technical deep-dive

Chloe — thanks for the clear summary. Quick responses inline below.

> 1) Connectivity preference: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering
We prefer PrivateLink for cross-account simplicity; security team likes endpoint isolation. Cross-account endpoints are fine for us as long as the endpoint service is whitelisted in our control plane.

> 2) Egress model
We intend to route outbound traffic from Redwood through our own NAT gateway (we manage egress). Important: we need to know any external IPs Redwood may call out to (for updates/telemetry). We'll populate the spreadsheet with our current egress plan.

> 3) IP allowlist
We'll fill the attached spreadsheet (sending after this reply) and include any /32s for control-plane callbacks.

> 4) TLS / mTLS
We require mTLS for inter-service connections inside the VPC; for Redwood <-> customer endpoint we prefer mTLS but can accept bearer token with short TTL if mTLS is challenging.

> 5) KMS / key handling
We use AWS KMS (multi-account key) and would prefer Redwood's private control plane to call our KMS via role-based access.

> 6) Audit & logs
Retention: 12 months. We'd like logs forwarded into our S3 bucket and a CloudWatch stream for near-real-time.

I'll have our network engineer, Priya Shah (priya.shah@aurelia.ai), pick a couple of times for the deep-dive and attach the partially filled egress spreadsheet.

Thanks — Daniel
Head of Platform, Aurelia Systems

[attachment: aurelia-egress-ips.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Daniel / Priya / Aurelia ops,

Appreciate the fast turnaround and useful answers — that's exactly what we needed to scope the implementation. Next actions from our side before the tech deep-dive: 

- Ben (SE) and Karthik (solutions) will prepare a draft network flow diagram based on your spreadsheet and the preference for PrivateLink + customer-managed NAT. I'll attach the first draft ahead of the call (expect a PNG).
- Ben will enumerate the static egress ranges Redwood will require for the Private control plane components (these are the ranges your firewall team needs to allow if you want callbacks to reach us).
- For mTLS, our Private deployment supports client cert upload to the appliance; we will confirm the cert exchange process and provide an example server cert rotation SOP.
- For KMS: we'll surface the role-based integration approach we use for AWS KMS in Private deployments (requires an IAM role in your account with sts:AssumeRole).

Can we lock the deep-dive for Thu 2027-07-15 10:00-11:00 PT? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a pre-read (network diagram + checklist). If not, please propose two alternate 2-hour windows next week.

Sending along the early network topology draft now.

Thanks,
Chloe
